quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: A dashed white line separates lanes going in the same direction. You can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Is it ever safe to drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under gates or barriers at a railroad crossing. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly.
Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep a steady speed. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: If your car skids on water, should you quickly apply the brakes?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your car skids while hydroplaning, release the accelerator and let the skid stop. Do not apply the brakes right away.

questions.question: How does distracted driving affect your reaction time?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
It makes you react more slowly to hazards.
It usually makes you drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes you react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before and while backing, turn your head to look through the rear window. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Change lanes to give it more space if you can do so safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to not block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both directions, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane ends ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use the brakes right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the road.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle can cross the center line to pass from either direction.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed frequently to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic, within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: At a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to combine into one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow diamonds with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming dangers. This sign means the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual sights. This causes traffic jams. Keep your attention on the road and drive carefully.

questions.question: You should increase the space between your car and the car ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger car.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When someone tailgates you, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly, as this can cause a crash.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to cars on your left or right.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars, bicycles, and pedestrians.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Running the engine while parked in the driveway.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every quick stop wastes fuel because you must accelerate again. Look ahead so you can slow down gradually or change lanes. This saves fuel and improves gas mileage.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads make it harder to stop and easier to skid on turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks if you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes the driver's hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes the driver's hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind off the road. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk by using a cell phone while driving.
